chunks.text: Hologram is a 100 Cyber fighter-only Extension, available in the first Campaign stage shop. Press 3: 2.5-second cooldown, two active, 15-second lifetime. It mirrors the owner's kit/appearance and apparent health, with no identifying outline or lean optimized model, even against Illusionist truth sight. It does not grant truth sight, spawn smoke or reset an existing visual track. On the first incoming hit it stops acting immediately and keeps a live-looking body during a 0.35-second smoothstep opacity fade; expiry uses the same fade. Incoming bullets and tool projectiles pass through visibly without being consumed/ghosted, and may hit a real fighter behind it. Outgoing shots, melee, spells and tools are cosmetic, pass through cover/fighters and cause no real/phantom damage, statuses, knockback, prop damage, crate rewards, shield drain, real grabs or debris consumption. Holograms do not count for victory; fading bodies cease contributing sight. Includes Normal imitation and free Generic selection in Equipment/Campaign, shared owner analysis and ordinary summon sight/search. Normal search remains learned-movement-only, without extra dodges or tactical navigation. Truth sight can identify ordinary Illusionist decoys, not Holograms or Shadows.

All Doppel, Shadow, Split and Illusionist fighter brains keep their own last-seen snapshots for up to six seconds, with Optimize illusions on or off. On losing team sight they drop the live target and use fixed observed coordinates, never unseen updates. Fresh visible acquisition refreshes the snapshot/timer; spawn-smoke identity resets still erase it immediately. Generic summons navigate toward the remembered point with ordinary jump/jet navigation, stop auto-firing at an unseen foe, and may loot currently visible power crates like normal AI. Normal imitation summons aim/search relative to their remembered point but move only with learned toward/away/still tendencies and learned jump/jet inputs, never automatic tactical movement or dodges. Learned blind fire is retained. Empty Normal profiles have no Generic fallback or automatic crate-looting policy. After six seconds without a sighting, the remembered point no longer drives searching. HP, damage, armor, cooldowns, prices and summon limits are unchanged.

A successful Illusionist FIGHTER cast produces a 0.65-second foreground smoke cloud covering the caster and new decoy. Ordinary enemy AI currently tracking the visible caster immediately loses its target, last-known identity and pending aim/fire lock, and reacquires at its next decision. This is a fresh acquisition, not a forced choice of decoy: the AI may pick the caster again without retaining original identity. Truth sight, allied/human observers, unrelated targets and unseen casts are unaffected. Prop/platform casts and failed casts (cooldown, active cap or invalid fighter construction) produce no spawn smoke or tracking reset. Smoke does not grant invulnerability, damage, collision or mechanical sight/projectile blocking. Prices, cooldowns, active limits and fighter lifetimes are unchanged.

Illusionist deception affects AI as well as displayed bars. Ordinary bots cannot identify real/decoy actors from hidden flags. They retain observed bodies while visually matching enemies stay separate; overlap or crossing can break the track, including between reaction ticks. Training improves retention without perfect immunity. When acquiring an uncertain group or losing a track, aggressive/Rusher selection is uniform among lookalikes, while Defender/Coverer/Support and cautious mind presets probabilistically favor nearer bodies. Continuous overlap does not reroll each tick. Losing sight drops live identity tracking; last-seen searches do not follow hidden coordinates. Full AI, lightweight summons and Normal imitation use these rules with Optimize illusions on or off, without giving Normal generic action policies. Phantom health affects retreat, threat assessment, equipment thresholds, support, finishing-target priority and tactical/owner-style hurt contexts. Real HP, death, damage links, healing, resources, rewards and real-damage learning evidence are untouched; ordinary phantom decay restores perceived health. Illusionist truth sight reads real HP and identifies illusion fighters, but does not reveal Shadows by hidden flags. Prices, active caps, cooldowns, hit budgets and lifetimes are unchanged.

Doppel, Shadow Clone, Split and Illusionist purchases include Normal imitation (default) plus free Generic fighter variants, including for existing owners. Select beneath the Extension in Equipment Bay or Campaign kit panel; the per-loadout choice changes brains only, not mechanics or Illusionist props/platforms. The generic tactical armor/equipment policies described elsewhere apply to Generic; Normal performs equipment actions only as learned from the owner. One recorder per owner observes input and context across every fight, even without a clone Extension. Human input habits persist locally; enemy/buddy owners learn only their own match behavior. Raw game intent and equipment states are batched at roughly 10 Hz. Context includes weapon kind, visible range, health, pressure and ground/air. Ready opportunities distinguish deliberate non-use from missing equipment/cooldowns. Store up to 64 contexts and 64 action-transition patterns with coarse quick/short/long gaps, never exact input timings. Summons share the owner's aggregate profile but do not train it. Normal reproduces omissions and mistakes: never-dodge remains no-dodge; jetpack overuse remains overuse. No success optimization, hidden-enemy knowledge, or extra Shadow caution. Each clone uses its own sight/resources/cooldowns and randomized decisions/timing, not synchronized input replay. Empty profiles wait for evidence, without a Generic fallback. Learning Lock freezes recording in all modes; tutorial is locked. Save locally every 15 match seconds, on quit and at match end. No external model or system-wide keyboard logging. Context notes describe associations, not proven intent. Generic keeps previous optimized/full AI, while Normal imitation is independent of Optimize illusions.

Player controls: A/D move, W or Space jump (hold airborne to jet), Shift jetpack thrust, C dodge/dash with brief invulnerability, Q raise/lower shield, F deploy/retract Retractable Armor or Shell, E cycle Mechanical Modularity modes (Sword → Shield → Pulse Rifle), mouse aim, left click fire/swing, G ping buddy, Escape pause.

Shadow Clone (280 Cyber): 3 spawns up to ten shadows with no cooldown; owner loses 100 max HP (20 in Classic). Persistent banks start full: 100 core HP in either mode and half the strongest owner shield maximum (dedicated shield or Modular plate, not their sum). Each clone base maximum is full core HP/shield capacity divided by living count. Only spawning redistributes bank + living current resources, capped at full pool capacity with excess discarded; banks empty. Bank regeneration never heals living clones. Unused capacity recharges at 20 HP/sec and 40% shield pool/sec (5s/2.5s from empty); capacity still deployed recharges at half speed. With 90 core HP deployed, first 10 bank HP takes 0.5s, then remaining 90 takes 9s. Banks may refill fully alongside living clones. Shift+3 banks the newest shadow's remaining core HP/shield without redistributing or healing owner/survivors; survivors gain maximum capacity, held props drop, effects do not transfer. Armor is independent and never redistributed, banked, or counted as deployed core HP. Death does not reset banks; spawning needs some core HP. Pause freezes recharge. Shadows share one shield allocation across Modular modes. Only allies see clone tells and actual HP; enemies see owner-matching bars and armor. Enemy Shadow Clone or Illusionist equipment does not reveal shadows. Actual shadow HP loss, including armor damage, transfers only to owner; direct owner HP loss affects all shadows without feedback. Effects, healing and timers are independent; new shadows inherit no effects. Split (300 Cyber): 3 spawns up to two persistent 250 core HP twins, including in Classic mode, 30s cooldown. H cycles control with 3s cooldown. Stored player HP and normal kit follow control with a 100 HP minimum, not 250; the abandoned body gets pre-switch HP capped at 250 core HP plus its existing deployed clone armor (without armor, 10 HP becomes a controlled 100 and an abandoned 10; 200 stays controlled 200 and leaves abandoned 200). Fuel, position, buffs, and debuffs stay with physical bodies. Real Doppel and Split twins use nanotech armor at 10% effectiveness and retractable armor at 85% strength; Shadow uses 5% nanotech and 10% retractable. Nanotech scales HP per bot and matching damage consumption, not weapon strength, bot supply, or recall. Generic twins top up nano armor in sustained fights and may deploy retractable shells alongside nanotech chestplates, with Optimize illusions on or off; Normal twins use learned owner input habits instead. Doppel, Shadow, Split and Illusionist include both variants at no extra cost. Illusionist fighters keep their existing armor effectiveness. Real twins cannot nest-spawn, survive the owner, or hold match victory.

Disguise (240 Cyber): 3 borrows an eligible real map breakable within 100 units, removing it from map cover and using its full appearance/hitbox. Walking is 55% speed. Remaining prop HP/bracing protects robot HP. Press 3, attack/use a weapon, or raise a shield to reveal and place that same prop at current feet. Breaking it reveals the robot and creates real debris there, never back at the original spot. Final-hit overkill does not spill into robot HP; barrel explosions still work. Five-second cooldown after reveal, no duration limit. No loot crates, illusions, held props, armor dummies, glare nodes, or Reconjurer-created props. Enemies see only the prop; allies see a subtle tell. AI can suspect repeated visible horizontal prop movement and test the observed position, without knowing hidden identity. Stationary disguises remain concealed; walls, visibility gaps, and stopping break or decay suspicion.

Jetpack: about 3 seconds continuous thrust from a full tank, about 5 seconds to recharge from empty while idle. Running dry engages exhausted lockout (HUD shows EXHAUSTED): thrust disabled until thrust input is fully released and fuel rebuilds to 20% restart reserve. Arena hard ceiling at y=12 world units; fighters clamp and projectiles leaving bounds are removed.

Shields are a separate equipment slot. Durability is a per-match block HP pool that normally does not recharge mid-match (Protective Rebuilding can refill it). Q raises the shield toward aim; only frontal cone attacks (~±70–80°) are blocked, spending durability equal to damage that would have been dealt. Cannot fire while raised. Depleted shields stay as dead weight with a stronger speed penalty until durability returns or the next match.

Learning is evidence-based with no automatic per-match XP for habits. Records change only when a relevant situation occurs, the buddy predicts or counters, and the result can be judged. Gun and saber profiles track engagement range, rush, dodge timing, jetpack use, and low-HP behavior separately. Learning Lock / Spar only stops Training from writing learning evidence; coaching goals can still be saved after a spar.

After Training, free-text coaching proposes practice goals. The buddy confirms interpretation before saving. Confirmed goals stay needs-practice until judged attempts support them. After Conquest the panel is Q&A only—no new practice goals. Deep answers still come only from local FAQ, manual chunks, or code-facts; the buddy never invents mechanics.

Conquest opens opponent select from Ranking league (Rookie through Apex). First reroll per visit is free; further rerolls cost 10¢ Cyber. Wins pay Cyber and Conquest EXP by reward tier (Rookie/Veteran/Elite); Ranking changes separately. Training and Spar pay no Cyber, Conquest EXP, or Ranking. Defeats remove no Cyber or EXP.

Equipment bay has five slots: body armor, helmet, weapon, jetpack, shield. Starter items are free; Shop unlocks purchases with Cyber for either teammate. Buddy gear autonomy: User Picked, AI Suggested, or AI's Choice. Perks unlock from Conquest EXP level-ups; each side equips at most one unlocked perk.

Arenas are fixed themed layouts (~3-screen width): Battlefield, City, Desert, Forest, Yard, Ruins, Docks. Breakable props have HP; intact soft cover blocks projectiles. Forest trunks are not solid for movement and do not hard-block vision. Props reset every match. Training can pick a map or Random; Conquest assigns mapId on encounter select.

Metal power-up crates are separate from wooden cover. The fighter who deals the killing blow gets the buff. Unseen crates are fog-hidden and not AI targets. Destroyed crates respawn after about 20s preferring unseen spots. Types include Fire Rate, Heal, Regen, Counter Slash, Speed Surge, Shield Patch, Jet Siphon, and Overcharge.

Flash, Balanced, and Thinker set mind ceilings for reaction tempo, aim turn rate, and risk style. Evidence earns anticipation up toward those ceilings. Mimic unlocks from readiness and copies learned player style with intensity Slight (~25%), Quite a bit (~55%), or Full (~85%). Conquest soft teammate-safety blend still limits mirror-suicide.

Fog of war hides unseen enemies. All living players, buddies, real Doppel/Shadow/Split clones, and Illusionist fighter decoys contribute normal equipped sight to shared team vision, even with Optimize illusions enabled. Summons expand fog coverage but obey sight range, directional weapon cones, map sight penalties, and walls. Their AI acquires only currently team-visible enemies, like a player, never unseen live coordinates. Full AI may search an unchanged remembered last-seen position. Dead summons contribute no sight. Optimization changes AI and draw detail, not sight rules. Cyan arrows cue off-screen threats; buddy outline helps track your partner. Soft cover and solid walls can block projectiles or sight depending on prop/map rules.

Language help is offline. MiniLM ranks local FAQ, manual, and code-fact snippets. Optional Gemma 3 270M may rewrite deep answers as a short blurb from those snippets only. Say you want a code based answer to force the code-facts pack. Nothing is downloaded at runtime and answers never invent combat rules outside local knowledge.
